# dsh-agent-team-ui-testing
**AI-native frontend GUI testing for DeepSeekHarness.**
Let AI agents operate, inspect, test and verify real user interfaces — with evidence humans can revi
AI agents operate, inspect, test and verify real user interfaces — with evidence humans can review.
**English** | 简体中文
> **Status: pre-release.** The Web/Chromium channel is implemented across all four tiers: 36 agent t
ools plus a debug panel for programmatic inspection, structured GUI actions, static visual analysis,
dynamic frame/timing analysis, network capture, multi-tab page groups, shared viewport control, a h
ybrid canvas, an element picker and client-side annotations. Other environments are planned and stay
disabled in the runtime picker. **Install:** `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-agent-team-ui-testin
g`. Capabilities, limits and verification are documented in docs/capability-tiers.md and docs/verifi
lities, limits and verification are documented in docs/capability-tiers.md and docs/verification.md.
## What is this?
**dsh-agent-team-ui-testing** is a UI testing infrastructure plugin for DeepSeekHarness (DSH). It le
ts an AI agent — or a coordinated Agent Team — drive a real application, inspect what the applicatio
n exposes, verify expected behavior, collect reviewable evidence and report actionable failures.
The runtime is built around a shared Chromium instance with one isolated page per DSH workspace, a t
yped tool surface, and a human-facing debug panel. The same session can be inspected programmaticall
y, operated through structured DOM/accessibility data, captured as screenshots, or analyzed visually
, operated through structured DOM/accessibility data, captured as screenshots, or analyzed visually.
The project grows out of the earlier `dsh-agent-team-browser` idea. The shared browser workspace rem
ains the first adapter of a broader, capability-aware UI testing runtime.
## Why build it?
Coding agents can produce UI code without being able to answer: **“Does the finished application act
ually work and look right?”** A 200 response, a running process or a single screenshot is not proof
of a working user journey.
This project focuses on:

- **Real UI feedback** — exercise user journeys on rendered interfaces, not only source code.
- **St
ructured-first automation** — prefer APIs, DOM and accessibility data; use vision when structure is

insufficient.
- **Evidence-based results** — record what ran, what was observed, what passed, what f

ailed and what remains unverified.
- **Human control** — authorized access, scoped sessions and a pa

nel humans can watch or take over.
- **Low disruption** — prefer background browser operations over
hijacking the desktop foreground.
## What works today
- **Shared browser runtime** — one browser per host and per runtime provider (the system Chrome/Chro
mium or Edge binary; the plugin does not bundle or install a browser), headless by default with an o
ptional headed mode in the Web view (off-screen hidden window + persistent profile); each DSH worksp
ace gets its own page, URL, viewport, history, network buffer and lease. Cookies and storage are sha

red by the profile of the active provider.
- **Runtime providers** — the web target environment defa
ults to `chrome` and also has a wired `edge` provider: its own executable candidates, its own `DSH_U
I_TESTING_EDGE` override, its own profile directory and a post-connect product-identity check, reusi
ng the same CDP stack. **A real Edge launch is not verified**: while Edge stays disabled its depende
ncy axis is `not-probed` (disabled providers are never probed); once enabled on a machine without an
Edge binary it reports `failed / executable-missing` on the Edge card, and enabling it opens no pag
e. In the settings page the group header is the target-environment switch and each card is a runtime
-provider switch; turning the total switch off greys the per-provider switches out while keeping the

ir saved values.
- **36 agent tools** across programmatic, structured GUI, static vision, dynamic be

havior, network debugging and per-workspace tab management.
- **Multi-tab page group (P0-E)** — each
workspace keeps a primary page plus up to three child tabs, with per-tab leases, per-agent tab sele

ction and popup adoption kept under the same isolation rules.
- **Dynamic behavior (T4)** — real CDP
screencast plus a screenshot-loop path, a bounded frame store with integrity counters, seven determ
inistic motion analyses, WAAPI motion control with restore, region-only frame delivery, and six-dire

ction frame↔network event correlation.
- **Debug panel** — live preview, responsive size controls, s
hared viewport state, a hybrid canvas, and a client-side annotation layer that agents can read back.

wport state, a hybrid canvas, and a client-side annotation layer that agents can read back.
[该节后续省略]
## Architecture design philosophy
> **In one sentence:** the AI agent decides *what to test and how to judge it*; the plugin *connects
, controls, observes, and preserves evidence*; and the target runtime *actually runs the application
*. **Web / Chromium is the implemented target today.** The three adapter contracts (`TargetAdapter`
/ `CapabilityAdapter` / `P0Provider`), the `core/` + `targets/` split, host-authoritative config, pe
r-step tool admission and environment-aware Skill discovery are implemented for Web; the `engines/`
boundary and other platform adapters remain planned.
### Capability architecture: choose T1 / T2 / T3 / T4 as needed
Tiers classify **testing methods and the evidence they can supply**. They are **selection and fallba
ck levels**, not a mandatory T1→T2→T3→T4 pipeline. Prefer the least expensive reliable method; escal
ate or combine methods only when the evidence is insufficient.
